title: Prime Ministers of India in Chronological Order (1947 – Present)
answer: Jawaharlal Nehru was the first and longest-serving Prime Minister of independent India (1947–1964). Prominent successors include Lal Bahadur Shastri ('Jai Jawan Jai Kisan'), Indira Gandhi (first female PM), Morarji Desai (first non-Congress PM), Rajiv Gandhi (youngest PM at age 40), P.V. Narasimha Rao (1991 economic reforms), Atal Bihari Vajpayee, Dr. Manmohan Singh, and Narendra Modi (2014–Present).
highlights: 1. Jawaharlal Nehru (1947–1964 — 16 years, 286 days, longest tenure)
2. Lal Bahadur Shastri (1964–1966 — Tashkent Agreement, Green/White revolution impetus)
3. Indira Gandhi (1966–1977, 1980–1984 — First and only female PM of India, 1971 Bangladesh Liberation War)
4. Morarji Desai (1977–1979 — First non-Congress Prime Minister, Janata Party)
5. Rajiv Gandhi (1984–1989 — Youngest PM at age 40; telecom & digital revolution pioneer)
6. P.V. Narasimha Rao (1991–1996 — Initiated LPG: Liberalisation, Privatisation, Globalisation reforms with FM Dr. Manmohan Singh)
7. Atal Bihari Vajpayee (1996, 1998–2004 — Pokhran-II nuclear tests, Golden Quadrilateral highways, Sarva Shiksha Abhiyan)
8. Dr. Manmohan Singh (2004–2014 — Two full terms; Indo-US Civil Nuclear Agreement, RTI Act, MNREGA)
9. Narendra Modi (2014–Present — 14th Prime Minister, Digital India, Make in India, GST, Jan Dhan, PM-KISAN)

title: Presidents of India in Chronological Order (1950 – Present)
answer: Dr. Rajendra Prasad was the first and longest-serving President of India (1950–1962). Notable successors include Dr. Sarvepalli Radhakrishnan, Dr. A.P.J. Abdul Kalam ('People's President'), Pratibha Patil (first female President), and Droupadi Murmu (first tribal woman President and current Head of State).
highlights: 1. Dr. Rajendra Prasad (1950–1962 — Longest serving, only President with two full terms)
2. Dr. S. Radhakrishnan (1962–1967 — Celebrated philosopher; birthday observed as Teachers' Day on 5 Sep)
3. Dr. Zakir Husain (1967–1969 — First Muslim President, first to die in office)
4. Neelam Sanjiva Reddy (1977–1982 — Youngest President at the time and only President elected unopposed)
5. K.R. Narayanan (1997–2002 — First Dalit President of India)
6. Dr. A.P.J. Abdul Kalam (2002–2007 — 11th President, renowned aerospace scientist & Bharat Ratna)
7. Pratibha Devisingh Patil (2007–2012 — 12th President, first woman President of India)
8. Droupadi Murmu (2022–Present — 15th President, first tribal woman President of India from Santhal community, Odisha)

title: Major Global Multilateral Groupings: G7, G20, BRICS & QUAD
answer: The G7 comprises seven advanced economies (USA, UK, Canada, France, Germany, Italy, Japan + EU). The G20 consists of 19 sovereign countries plus the European Union and the African Union (inducted at New Delhi Summit 2023). BRICS was founded by Brazil, Russia, India, China, and South Africa (expanded in 2024 to include Egypt, Ethiopia, Iran, UAE). The QUAD is a security dialogue comprising India, the US, Japan, and Australia.
highlights: G7 (Group of Seven): United States, United Kingdom, Canada, France, Germany, Italy, Japan, and the European Union

G20 (Group of Twenty): 19 countries (Argentina, Australia, Brazil, Canada, China, France, Germany, India, Indonesia, Italy, Japan, South Korea, Mexico, Russia, Saudi Arabia, South Africa, Turkey, UK, USA) + European Union + African Union
BRICS: Brazil, Russia, India, China, South Africa + new members (Egypt, Ethiopia, Iran, United Arab Emirates)
QUAD (Quadrilateral Security Dialogue): India, United States, Japan, Australia (ensuring a free, open, and prosperous Indo-Pacific)
SCO (Shanghai Cooperation Organisation): Intergovernmental Eurasian alliance founded in 2001 (HQ Beijing, China; India joined in 2017)

title: Principal United Nations (UN) Specialized Agencies & Headquarters
answer: Principal UN specialized agencies and their global headquarters include: WHO (World Health Organization — Geneva, Switzerland), UNESCO (Paris, France), UNICEF (New York City, USA), IMF & World Bank (Washington, D.C., USA), WTO (Geneva, Switzerland), FAO (Rome, Italy), and the International Court of Justice (ICJ — Peace Palace, The Hague, Netherlands).
highlights: WHO (World Health Organization): Headquarters in Geneva, Switzerland (founded 7 April 1948)
UNESCO: Headquarters in Paris, France (educational, scientific, and cultural heritage promotion)
UNICEF (UN Children's Fund): Headquarters in New York City, USA
IMF (International Monetary Fund) & World Bank: Headquarters in Washington, D.C., USA (Bretton Woods Institutions, 1944)
WTO (World Trade Organization): Headquarters in Geneva, Switzerland (established 1995 replacing GATT)
FAO (Food and Agriculture Organization): Headquarters in Rome, Italy
ICJ (International Court of Justice): Principal judicial organ of the UN, situated at the Peace Palace in The Hague, Netherlands

title: UN Security Council Permanent Members (P5) & Veto Power
answer: The United Nations Security Council (UNSC) has 5 permanent members (P5): the United States, the United Kingdom, France, Russia, and China. Under the UN Charter, each of the P5 members possesses an absolute veto power over substantive Security Council resolutions.
highlights: P5 Members: United States, United Kingdom, France, Russian Federation (inherited from USSR), People's Republic of China
Total UNSC Strength: 15 members (5 Permanent members + 10 Non-Permanent members elected for 2-year terms by the UN General Assembly)
Veto Power: A negative vote by any single permanent member invalidates a substantive resolution, regardless of overall majority support
G4 Nations: India, Brazil, Germany, and Japan mutually support each other's bids for permanent seats on an expanded UNSC

title: First in India — Historical Pioneers & Milestones
answer: Historical firsts in independent India include: Rakesh Sharma (first Indian in space, 1984), Kiran Bedi (first female IPS officer, 1972), Abhinav Bindra (first Indian to win an individual Olympic gold medal in 10m Air Rifle, Beijing 2008), and Justice M. Fathima Beevi (first female judge of the Supreme Court of India, 1989).
highlights: First Indian in Space: Wing Commander Rakesh Sharma (3 April 1984 on Soviet Soyuz T-11; described India from space as 'Saare Jahan Se Achha')
First Woman IPS Officer: Dr. Kiran Bedi (joined Indian Police Service in 1972; Ramon Magsaysay Award winner)
First Individual Olympic Gold: Abhinav Bindra (Beijing 2008 Men's 10m Air Rifle shooting)
First Woman Judge of Supreme Court: Justice M. Fathima Beevi (appointed in October 1989)
First Chief Justice of India: Justice Harilal Jekisundas Kania (1950–1951)
First Chief Election Commissioner of India: Sukumar Sen (1950–1958, conducted first two general elections)
